name: Champorado
difficultyReason: One pot; stir regularly to prevent sticking.
steps: Rinse the glutinous rice and drain.
Put rice and 600 ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then lower to a gentle simmer.
Mix cocoa with a little hot cooking liquid until smooth. Stir it into the pot with the sugar.
Cook for about 20–25 minutes, stirring frequently, until the rice is soft. Add water as needed; finish with evaporated milk.

name: Maja blanca
difficultyReason: Control thickening, then allow the pudding to chill.
steps: Whisk the cornstarch into one quarter of the cold coconut milk until smooth.
Gently heat the remaining coconut milk, coconut cream, condensed milk and sugar in a saucepan.
Whisk in the slurry. Stir continuously over low heat for 10–15 minutes until thick, smooth and bubbling gently.
Spoon into a shallow container. Refrigerate promptly and let it set for at least one hour before cutting.
notes: Time includes at least 60 minutes chilling. Refrigerate leftovers. Contains milk; check all product labels.

name: Lumpiang Shanghai
difficultyReason: Prepare an even filling, roll tightly and control frying heat.
steps: Finely grate carrot and mince garlic. Mix with pork and beaten egg; keep the raw filling chilled while preparing the wrappers.
Divide filling between wrappers in thin logs. Fold the sides inward, roll firmly, and seal the edges with a little water.
Heat oil in a deep, heavy pan to about 170°C. Keep the pan less than half full and fry small batches, turning carefully.
Cook until crisp and the center of the filling reaches 71°C. Check with a thermometer; a brown wrapper does not prove the meat is cooked.
Drain on a rack and serve with banana ketchup.
notes: Oil is a pan allowance, not the amount eaten. Use enough for your pan while keeping it less than half full; do not multiply oil depth when increasing servings.

name: Kare-kare
difficultyReason: Coordinate a long braise, separate vegetables and a thickened peanut sauce.
steps: Cover oxtail with about 1.2 litres water in a heavy pot. Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer gently for 2½–3 hours or until fork-tender. Add hot water to keep it covered.
Soak annatto seeds in 100 ml warm water, then strain and discard the seeds.
Slice eggplant, trim beans and slice the tender prepared banana blossom. Boil the vegetables separately until tender and drain.
Soften chopped onion and garlic in oil. Add annatto liquid, ground peanuts, toasted rice flour and enough oxtail broth to make a smooth sauce.
Simmer while stirring until thickened. Fold in the tender meat and vegetables, add fish sauce and heat through. Thin with broth as needed.
notes: Contains peanuts and fish. Chef level describes coordination, not professional certification. Prepared banana blossom has tough outer layers removed.

name: Paksiw na bangus
difficultyReason: A gentle one-pot simmer using fish already cleaned by the fishmonger.
steps: Use scaled, fully gutted milkfish cut into steaks. Check for bones; slice carrot and deseeded bitter melon.
Arrange vegetables, crushed garlic and chili in a saucepan, then place fish on top.
Add salt, pepper, vinegar and 120 ml water. Bring to a gentle boil, cover, then lower the heat.

Simmer gently for about 15–20 minutes, until vegetables are tender and fish reaches 63°C at its thickest part. Add a little water if the pan becomes dry. Serve carefully; milkfish has many fine bones.

name: Chicken sopas
difficultyReason: One pot; add vegetables and milk in stages.
steps: Dice boneless chicken and carrot; chop onion, garlic and cabbage.
Warm oil in a saucepan. Soften onion and garlic, then add chicken, salt and pepper.
Add 600 ml water. Bring to a boil and simmer for about 10 minutes.
Add macaroni and carrot. Simmer according to the pasta packet, adding cabbage for the final few minutes. Check that chicken reaches 74°C.
Lower the heat and stir in evaporated milk. Warm gently without a vigorous boil and serve promptly; add water if the pasta absorbs too much broth.

name: Pinakbet
difficultyReason: Add vegetables in stages so each becomes tender.
steps: Chop onion and tomatoes, mince garlic, and cut vegetables into even bite-size pieces. Remove bitter melon seeds.
Warm oil and soften onion and garlic. Add tomatoes and shrimp paste; cook for five minutes.
Add sweet potato, bitter melon and 100 ml water. Cover and simmer until almost tender, checking the pan does not dry out.
Add beans, eggplant and okra. Cover and cook until all vegetables are tender, stirring gently. Serve as a side; rice is separate.
notes: Contains shellfish from shrimp paste; this version is not vegetarian.

name: Nilagang baka
difficultyReason: Straightforward simmering, with a long wait for tender beef.
steps: Put beef ribs, quartered onion, pepper and salt in a pot with about 1.2 litres water. Bring to a boil and skim the surface.
Lower the heat and simmer for 2–2½ hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Top up water to keep the meat covered.
Cut corn into sections and potatoes into chunks. Add them with peeled, sliced saba and simmer until tender, about 15–20 minutes.
Add cabbage, bok choy and sliced spring onion. Simmer until the greens are cooked and serve with the broth.

name: Turon with caramel
difficultyReason: Seal the rolls, manage hot oil, then coat in hot caramel.
steps: Peel saba and cut each lengthwise into four pieces. Place one piece on each wrapper.
Fold the sides in, roll snugly, and seal with a little water. Keep the outside dry.
Heat oil to about 170°C in a heavy pan kept less than half full. Fry in small batches until golden and the banana is tender; drain on a rack.
In a separate heavy pan, gently heat brown sugar until melted. Remove from heat and turn the rolls in the caramel using tongs.
Let the coating cool before eating. Hot caramel causes severe burns; do not touch it or add water to hot oil.
notes: Oil is a pan allowance, not the amount eaten. Do not multiply oil depth when scaling; cook in batches. Chef level reflects hot caramel handling.

name: Bicol Express
difficultyReason: Simmer pork until tender while keeping coconut sauce from scorching.
steps: Cut pork belly into small cubes. Chop onion, garlic and chilies; wash hands after handling chili and avoid touching your eyes.
Warm oil and soften onion and garlic. Add pork and cook, turning, until lightly browned.
Stir in shrimp paste, chilies, sugar and pepper. Add coconut milk and 100 ml water.
Simmer gently for about 40–50 minutes until pork is tender, stirring and adding water if needed. Check pork reaches at least 63°C with a three-minute rest; continue cooking for tenderness.
notes: Contains shellfish. Chili heat varies; use fewer chilies for a milder dish.

name: Pork binagoongan with shrimp
difficultyReason: Braise pork first, then time the vegetables and shrimp.
steps: Cut pork into small cubes. Chop onion and tomatoes, mince garlic, and slice deseeded bitter melon. Keep peeled, deveined shrimp refrigerated.
Heat oil in a saucepan and brown the pork. Add onion, garlic and tomatoes; cook until the onion softens.
Add shrimp paste, vinegar and 250 ml water. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 40–50 minutes until pork is tender, adding water if needed.
Add bitter melon and cook until tender. Add shrimp near the end and cook until pearly and opaque throughout. Check pork doneness before serving.
notes: Contains shellfish. This source variation includes shrimp and bitter melon. Rice is separate; shrimp paste saltiness varies by brand.

name: Lechon paksiw
difficultyReason: Gently simmer already-cooked pork and thicken the sauce.
steps: Use safely refrigerated, boneless roast pork leftovers. Cut into bite-size pieces. Slice the tender prepared banana blossom and crush garlic.
Place pork, garlic, pepper, sugar, banana blossom and bay leaf in a pot with 300 ml water. Bring to a boil and simmer gently for about 25 minutes.
Add vinegar, soy sauce and liver sauce. Simmer for 10–15 minutes, stirring and adding water if the sauce becomes too thick.
Mix cornstarch with a little cold water. Stir into the simmering sauce and cook until thickened. Reheat the pork to 74°C throughout. Remove bay leaf before serving.
notes: Requires cooked roast pork, not raw pork. Use leftovers refrigerated promptly; reheating does not make spoiled or improperly stored food safe. Check liver sauce ingredients for allergens.

name: Filipino-style spaghetti
difficultyReason: Coordinate a meat sauce with pasta cooked in a separate pot.
steps: Slice hot dogs, chop onion and garlic, and grate cheese. Heat oil in a pan, brown hot dogs and lift onto a plate.
Soften onion in the same pan. Add garlic and pork mince, breaking the meat into small pieces as it cooks.

Stir in tomato paste, then return hot dogs. Add banana ketchup, tomato puree, chicken stock and soy sauce. Simmer for 10–15 minutes, stirring frequently. Check the pork reaches 71°C and follow hot-dog package heating instructions.
Meanwhile, boil spaghetti according to its packet and drain. Toss with the hot sauce, divide between bowls and top with cheese.
notes: Contains meat and dairy; pasta and soy sauce commonly contain wheat. Check hot-dog and sauce labels. Use dry spaghetti; cooked pasta is not equivalent by weight.

name: Kwek-kwek
difficultyReason: Coat cooked quail eggs and fry small batches at a controlled temperature.
steps: Start with hard-cooked, peeled quail eggs. Pat their surfaces dry.
Mix flour and food-grade annatto powder. Whisk in cool water gradually, starting with 60 ml and adding just enough to make a thick coating batter.
Heat oil to about 180°C in a deep heavy pan kept less than half full. Coat the eggs in batter and carefully lower small batches into the oil.
Fry until the coating is cooked and lightly golden and the eggs are hot throughout. Drain on a rack and allow to cool slightly before eating.
notes: Contains eggs and wheat. Time starts with cooked eggs. Oil is a pan allowance, not consumption; keep the pan less than half full and cook in batches instead of multiplying oil depth. Dipping sauce is separate.

name: Sinigang na baboy
difficultyReason: Simmer pork until tender and add vegetables in stages.
steps: Cut pork into bite-size cubes. Quarter onion and tomatoes; slice radish, trim beans and wash water spinach.
Put pork, onion and tomatoes in a pot with 900 ml water. Bring to a boil, skim and simmer for 45–60 minutes until pork is tender. Add water to maintain the broth.
Add radish and beans. Simmer until tender, then stir in seedless tamarind paste, fish sauce and the whole green chili.
Add water spinach and cook until tender. Check pork doneness. Taste and adjust the sourness gradually, as tamarind strength varies.
notes: Contains fish sauce. Tamarind paste varies in concentration; begin with part of the listed amount and taste. Soup mix is not equivalent to pure tamarind paste; follow its package directions if adapting.
